questions.q: A sportsman runs around a circular track of radius $r$ such that he traverses the path $A B A B$. The distance travelled and displacement, respectively, are
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Displacement $=2 r$
Distance $=2 \pi r+\pi r=3 \pi r$

questions.q: A particle of mass <math><mi>m</mi></math> and charge <math><mi>q</mi></math> is released from rest in a uniform electric field. If there is no other force on the particle, the dependence of its speed <math><mi>v</mi></math> on the distance <math><mi>x</mi></math> travelled by it is correctly given by (graphs are schematic and not drawn to scale)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The particle is at rest initially.

So, the initial velocity u=0 m s-1.

The force on the charged particle in the uniform electric field,

F=qE

⇒ ma=qE

⇒ a=qEm

Applying the velocity-displacement equation under constant acceleration,

v2=u2+2ax

⇒ v2=02+2qEmx

⇒ v2=2qEmx

=3-23+2

questions.q: A small steel ball is dropped into a long cylinder containing glycerine. Which one of the following is the correct representation of the velocity time graph for the transit of the ball?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Consider a small steel ball as shown below:

As shown in diagram, buoyancy force FB=F.

Applying Newton's second law, we get

mg-FB-Fv=ma

⇒ρ43πr3g-ρL43πr3g-6πηrv=mdvdt

Let 43mπR3gρ-ρL=K1 and 6πηrm=K2, then we get

⇒dvdt=K1-K2v

Integrating both sides, we get

⇒∫0vdvK1-K2v=∫0tdt

⇒-1K2lnK1-K2v0v=t

⇒lnK1-K2vK1=-K2t

⇒K1-K2v=K1e-K2t

⇒v=K1K21-e-K2t

questions.q: Two buses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> start from a point at the same time and move in a straight line and their positions are represented by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mfenced><mi>t</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mfenced><mi>t</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. At what time, both the buses have same velocity ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, v=dxdt.

Given, xPt=αt+βt2

Velocity of bus P is vP=dxPdt=α+2βt and velocity of bus Q is vQ=f-2t

When vP=vQ

⇒α+2βt=f-2t

 ⇒f-α=2β+1t ⇒t=f-α2β+1

questions.q: An object moves with speed v1, v2 and v3 along a line segment AB, BC and CD respectively as shown in figure. Where AB = BC and AD = 3 AB, then average speed of the object will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Speed of an object is defined as the distance travelled by the object per unit time.

Let's assume that, AB= d. So, BC= d, AD= 3d. Also, assume that the time required by the object to travel AB, BC, CD are t1, t2, t3 respectively.

Now,

AD= 3ABAB+BC+CD= 3ABAB+AB+CD= 3ABCD= AB

Hence,

t1= ABv1= dv1t2= dv2t3= dv3

The formula to calculate the average speed va of the object is given by

va= ADt1+t2+t3........................(1)

Substitute the expressions for the parameters into equation (1) and simplify to obtain the required average speed of the object.

va= 3ddv1+dv2+dv3= 3v1v2v3v1v2+v2v3+v3v1

questions.q:
The position-time graphs for two students A and B returning from the school to their homes are shown in figure.

(A) A lives closer to the school

(B) B lives closer to the school

(C) A takes lesser time to reach home

(D) A travels faster than B

(E) B travels faster than A

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the position time graph the velocity is found out by the slope of the line. The slope is given by x2-x1t2-t1.

The slope of B is greater than A. Hence, the velocity of B is greater than A. As can be seen from the graph XA<XB. So A lives closer to the school and VB>VA. Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically up (taken as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> ) from the ground. The correct momentum-height <math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo>)</mo></math> diagram is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If the ball was thrown with initial velocity u , then its velocity at height 'h' can be written as.
v=u2-2gh
Its linear momentum, p=mv=mu2-2gh
Or  p2=m2u2-2m2gh
The graph between p & h will be a parabola.
In motion when particle was going up, its velocity is positive and decreasing with height and so is the linear momentum. When it reaches the maximum height, the velocity and linear momentum will be zero. Again, it will start to fall back, the velocity and linear momentum will increase but will have negative value.

questions.q: Water droplets are coming from an open tap at a particular rate. The spacing between a droplet observed at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> second after its fall to the next droplet is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>34</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. At what rate the droplets are coming from the tap ? (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In 4th sec, 1st drop will travel 

⇒12×9.8×42=78.4 m

∴ 2nd drop would have travelled

⇒78.4-34.3=44.1 m

Time for 2nd drop

129.8t2=44.1

t=3 sec

∴ Each drop have time gap of 1 sec.

∴ 1 drop per second.

questions.q: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mfenced><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mfenced><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that t=x+4

⇒x=t-42=t2-8t+16

Differentiating the above equation with respect to time,

⇒dxdt=2t-8

Putting the value of t=4

⇒dxdt=2×4−8=0

questions.q: A particle is moving in a straight line. The variation of position <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> as a function of time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is given as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The velocity of the body when its acceleration becomes zero is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given the instantaneous position is

x=t3-6t2+20t+15   ...1

The velocity of the particle is given by

v=dxdt=3t2-12t+20   ...2

And, the acceleration of the particle is given by

a=dvdt=6t-12   ...3

When a=0, it implies

6t-12=0⇒t=2 s

At t=2 s, the velocity can be calculated as follows:

v=3(2)2-12(2)+20=8 m s-1

questions.q: A body projected vertically upwards with a certain speed from the top of a tower reaches the ground in $t_1$. If it is projected vertically downwards from the same point with the same speed, it reaches the ground in $t_2$. Time required to reach the ground, if it is dropped from the top of the tower, is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{t}_1=\frac{\mathrm{u}+\sqrt{\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{gh}}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ & \mathrm{t}_2=\frac{-\mathrm{u}+\sqrt{\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{gh}}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ & \mathrm{t}=\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gh}}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ & \mathrm{t}_1 \mathrm{t}_2=\frac{\left(\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{gh}\right)-\mathrm{u}^2}{\mathrm{~g}^2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{gh}}{\mathrm{g}^2}=\mathrm{t}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\mathrm{t}_1 \mathrm{t}_2}\end{aligned}$

a=-(2m)v3

questions.q: A horse rider covers half the distance with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> speed. The remaining part of the distance was travelled with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for half the time and with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for other half of the time. The mean speed of the rider averaged over the whole time of motion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let total distance travelled by horse rider be 2x.

Now, the time taken to cover first half distance is tAB=x5

Second half distance x between BC is covered in two parts, x=d1+d2

here d1 is the distance travelled with 10  m s-1 and d2 is the distance travelled with 15 m s-1 in equal time intervals t2 each.

Then, d1=10t2, d2=15t2

Second half distance x=t2(10+15)=25t2

Now, the mean speed of rider is v=2xx5+2x25=2×255+2=507  m s-1

Thus, the value of x=50.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>19</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> from the top of a tower. The ball strikes the ground after <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The height from the ground up to which the ball can rise will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> is _____ (use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial velocity of ball is u=19.6 m s-1, final velocity v=0.

Using v=u+at, here, acceleration a=-g.

Time taken in upward motion above tower is ta=ug=19.69.8=2 s

Now, time taken from top most point to ground is td=6-2=4 s.

Or, td=2hmaxg    (Using s=ut+12gt2)

⇒hmax=16×9.82=3925 m.

Hence, the value of k=392.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:

Instantaneous acceleration of the particle can be written as, a=vdvdx

=4x×4×12x-1/2=8 m s-2

questions.q: The maximum speed of a boat in still water is \(27 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}\). Now this boat is moving downstream in a river flowing at \(9 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}\). A man in the boat throws a ball vertically upwards with speed of \(10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\). Range of the ball as observed by an observer at rest on the river bank, is _______ cm. (Take \(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\))
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{b}}=9+27=36 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
$\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{b}}=36 \times \frac{1000}{36000}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{sec} \\ & \text { Time of flight }=\frac{2 \times 10}{10}=2 \mathrm{sec} \\ & \text { Range }=10 \times 2=20 \mathrm{~m}=2000 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement $x$ at any time $t$ is given by $x^2=1+t^2$. Its acceleration at any time $\mathrm{t}$ is $x^{-\mathrm{n}}$ where $\mathrm{n}=$ ___________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}^2=1+\mathrm{t}^2 \\ & 2 \mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \mathrm{t} \\ & \mathrm{xv}=\mathrm{t} \\ & \mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{v} \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=1 \\ & \mathrm{x} \cdot \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{v}^2=1 \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{1-\mathrm{v}^2}{\mathrm{x}}=\frac{1-\mathrm{t}^2 / \mathrm{x}^2}{\mathrm{x}} \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}=\mathrm{x}^{-3}\end{aligned}$
